# Measured conversions between definitions

*Generated by `scripts/make-conversions-doc.py` from `data/conversions.json`; do not edit by hand.*

When two curves use different definitions (all bound stars or a 2 R_half aperture, SFR of all gas or of the disc, M200crit or the total Subfind mass), by how much does the number change? Instead of assuming, this page reports what the **public CAMELS catalogues** show: for each of three codes (IllustrisTNG, SIMBA, Astrid), 27 fiducial-model boxes of 25 Mpc/h (total comoving volume 1,395,796 Mpc³ per code), read with `scripts/ingest_camels_conversions.py`. Each cell is the **median change in log10 of the quantity, with the 16th to 84th percentile of galaxies in square brackets and the standard error across the 27 boxes after ±**. A negative number means the second definition gives a smaller value.

## How to read and how not to use these numbers

- These describe **these three codes at this resolution and box size**. The three codes disagree with one another (see the tables), which is the point: there is no single aperture correction that fits every simulation, so the Explorer does not apply one. A reader who wants to correct a particular curve should measure it for the code that made it.
- Only apertures that the catalogues provide are covered: all bound particles, twice the stellar half-mass radius, the stellar half-mass radius and the radius of maximum circular velocity. Fixed physical apertures (30 or 50 kpc), projected apertures, survey fibres and SED-fitted total masses are not in the catalogues and are not covered.
- The catalogue documentation defines the aperture fields as sums over **all particles or cells within the radius**, and the total fields as the particles **bound to the subhalo** ([TNG data specification](https://www.tng-project.org/data/docs/specifications/)). The two can therefore differ for reasons other than the aperture (for example unbound stars inside the radius). We report the difference as measured.
- The aperture SFR is documented as the total SFR "restricted to cells within twice the stellar half mass radius", so it should not exceed the total; the medians here are slightly positive (below +0.02 dex in every bin published; checked by `scripts/test_camels_conversions.py`), which means the two fields are not an exact subset relation in these catalogues. We have not traced why; the effect is far smaller than the other numbers.
- No resolution test has been run, so differences between the codes, especially at the low-mass end, could partly be resolution rather than physics.
- Galaxies for which either quantity is exactly zero are left out of the median and counted in the zero-fraction column of `data/conversions.json`.

## What it does to a mass function

The change in a stellar mass function is not the median shift, because galaxies change mass by different amounts and the function is steep. We therefore rebuilt the mass function of each code from each mass definition and measured the **horizontal shift in log10 M\* at fixed cumulative number density** (the mass above which a given number of galaxies per Mpc³ lie), with the standard error across boxes.

| code | conversion | n(>M) = 10^-2 | 10^-2.5 | 10^-3 | 10^-3.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IllustrisTNG | 2 R_half aperture | -0.09 ± 0.002 | -0.10 ± 0.002 | -0.12 ± 0.003 | -0.14 ± 0.004 |
| IllustrisTNG | R(V_max) aperture | -0.12 ± 0.005 | -0.11 ± 0.004 | -0.13 ± 0.006 | -0.09 ± 0.006 |
| SIMBA | 2 R_half aperture | -0.09 ± 0.001 | -0.09 ± 0.002 | -0.10 ± 0.002 | -0.10 ± 0.003 |
| SIMBA | R(V_max) aperture | -0.37 ± 0.002 | -0.54 ± 0.004 | -0.61 ± 0.004 | -0.60 ± 0.009 |
| Astrid | 2 R_half aperture | -0.05 ± 0.001 | -0.05 ± 0.001 | -0.06 ± 0.003 | -0.10 ± 0.003 |
| Astrid | R(V_max) aperture | -0.06 ± 0.002 | -0.03 ± 0.002 | -0.02 ± 0.002 | -0.02 ± 0.003 |

Densities are in Mpc⁻³; the volume is small, so the highest-mass column (10^-3.5) rests on few galaxies per box.

## Where the numbers come from

`data/ensembles/camels-conversions.json` holds the per-box medians and counts and the pooled histograms; the SHA-256 of the catalogue arrays read is in `data/conversions.json` (`arraysSha256`, per code and snapshot). Retrieved 2026-10-20. Source: CAMELS first-generation Subfind catalogues (Villaescusa-Navarro et al. 2021, ApJ 915, 71), cosmic-variance set CV.
